text: No, the sources contradict each other on the 2012 tree-cover loss. Hansen GFC detected 1.4 ha of loss, but the JRC 2020 reference map—used as an independent check—only agrees with 49% of that area. Since the system requires at least 50% agreement for corroboration, the evidence is insufficient to confirm the loss. Additionally, MGAP’s 2021 forest map shows no native forest in the affected area, with only 0.4 ha of planted forest, suggesting the change may not have been significant deforestation. The sources thus disagree on whether meaningful tree-cover loss occurred.
